description.value: The study examined cerebral responses to visual photographs of high-calorie foods, low-calorie foods, and nonedible dining-related utensils in healthy normal-weight women.

spans.text: Therefore, we applied functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to study the cerebral responses of 13 healthy normal-weight adult women as they viewed color photographs of food.

design.value: A within-subjects fMRI visual activation study with three separate counterbalanced scanning runs, comparing high-calorie foods, low-calorie foods, and nonedible food-related utensils against nonfood control images.

spans.text: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs: (1) low-calorie foods, (2) high-calorie foods, and (3) nonedible food-related utensils.
The order of presentation of the three tasks was counterbalanced across subjects.
